rules.svo: English word order is fixed: subject → verb → object. Time and place go at the end.
rules.be: English never drops the linking verb: the parcel IS late, I AM happy.
rules.present3: He, she, it and any singular subject take -s: the shop opens, my sister works.
rules.past: A finished past action needs a past form: I bought, we went, she sent.
rules.perfect: Present Perfect links the past to now: I have sent, she has arrived.
rules.future: Plans and promises take will or going to + the base form of the verb.
rules.article: A singular countable noun needs an article: a phone, an email, the receipt.
rules.plural: After a number or 'many', a countable noun stays plural: two emails, many people.
rules.prep: Prepositions are fixed by phrase, not by logic: on Monday, in May, at 6 p.m.
rules.modal: After can, should, must and will the verb has no 'to': I can send, you should write.
rules.adv: Adverbs describe the verb and usually end in -ly: he answered quickly.
rules.question: A question inverts the order: Could you…? Do you…? Have you…?
rules.negative: One negative is enough, and it needs an auxiliary: I do not have any time.
rules.linker: A linking word at the start of a sentence takes a comma: However, the parcel was late.
rules.relative: Use who for people and that/which for things: the parcel that arrived late.
rules.gerund: After a preposition the verb takes -ing: look forward to hearing, instead of paying.
rules.conditional: In an if-clause English uses the present, not will: If it rains, I will stay at home.
rules.passive: The passive is be + third form: the box was damaged, the report is written.
rules.compare: One comparative at a time: better, not more better; cheaper, not more cheaper.
rules.quantifier: Many with countable nouns, much with uncountable: many emails, much information.

fnWhy.Opening: Without an opening line the reader does not know what the text is for.
fnWhy.Greeting: The greeting sets the distance between you and the reader in three words.
fnWhy.Giving facts: Facts the reader can check are what make a text useful.
fnWhy.Describing: Details are what the reader remembers; general words disappear.
fnWhy.Giving opinion: An opinion marked as an opinion is stronger than a bare statement.
fnWhy.Contrasting: Showing the other side proves you thought about it.
fnWhy.Asking: A clear question is the only way to get a clear answer.
fnWhy.Requesting: A request with a verb and a deadline gets an answer; a hint does not.
fnWhy.Explaining: The reason is what turns a complaint into a case.
fnWhy.Closing: The last line decides what the reader does next.

howto.word-order: Tap the words in the right order — they move into the line. Tap a word in the line to send it back. English word order is fixed, so the order itself carries the meaning.
howto.transform: Read the sentence and the instruction next to it. Write your own version: same meaning, different form. The model answer appears after you check.
howto.connectors: The linking words are in the bank at the top. Tap a linking word, then tap the gap — or drag it with the mouse. Each word is used once.
howto.punctuation: Rewrite the sentence with capital letters and punctuation. Do not change the words themselves.
howto.expand: Turn the notes into a full sentence: add articles, prepositions and the right verb form. Keep the meaning.
howto.register: The same idea, two versions. Choose the one that fits the reader. Register is not about being polite — it is about distance.
howto.idea-bank: Sort the ideas into two columns: what goes into your text and what only waters it down. Then choose the three strongest ideas.
howto.outline-builder: Put the blocks into the four parts of the text. The checker knows the logic of the genre: some blocks cannot stand where you put them.
howto.guided-write: Answer one question at a time, in English, one or two sentences. At the end your answers become a draft in the Writing Pad. The hints are questions, not ready sentences: the text stays yours.
howto.free-write: Now the whole text, on your own. The Writing Pad gives you the checklist, the phrase bank, the linking words and your plan. The timer is optional.
howto.overall: This is the site's own summary of the genre. It counts the exercises you have finished, how accurate you were, and the scores of the text you submitted, and turns all of that into one band. Nothing here is a school grade — it only shows what to work on next.
